Q0564

“The knowledge of anything that has causes is not complete unless it…” — Avicenna (The Healing, Metaphysics I)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: The Healing, Metaphysics I. Theme: knowledge.

Quotes / Avicenna / Q0564

The knowledge of anything that has causes is not complete unless it is known through its causes.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to The Healing, Metaphysics I and files it under Islamic Philosophy. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Avicenna

Ibn Sīnā (Avicenna, 980–1037) wrote The Healing and The Canon of Medicine, dominating Islamic and later Latin curricula. Born near Bukhara, he synthesized Aristotelian and Neoplatonic themes into a system centered on the Necessary Existent and an immortal rational soul.

How to read this passage

Epistemology asks whether knowledge is justified true belief, reliable tracking of the world, or something else; it also asks how perception, testimony, memory, and reason contribute. This passage enters that discussion through knowledge.

Concepts in this quote

Knowledge
Knowledge is the philosophical study of what we can justifiably claim to know—and where certainty ends.
